q: Rivalry in amassing wealth has made you negligent
v.c: Competition for more ˹gains˺ diverts you ˹from Allah˺,

q: ...(and this rivalry will continue making you negligent)
(when you die). (It is only when a person dies that he realises the futility of amassing wealth because none of it will benefit him in the Aakhirah.)
v.c: until you end up in ˹your˺ graves.

q: Soon you will come to know
v.s: No! You are going to know.
v.c: But no! You will soon come to know.

q: (This rivalry will most certainly not benefit you, but)
You will soon come to know
v.s: Then, no! You are going to know.
v.c: Again, no! You will soon come to know.

q: (about the eventual reality, you would not have preoccupied yourself with this rivalry to accumulate wealth).
v.s: No! If you only knew with knowledge of certainty...
v.c: Indeed, if you were to know ˹your fate˺ with certainty, ˹you would have acted differently˺.

q: (By Allaah! Because of your preoccupation with this rivalry to amass wealth.)
v.s: You will surely see the Hellfire.
v.c: ˹But˺ you will surely see the Hellfire.

q: You will then surely see it with the eye of certainty
(when you will be unable to deny its existence).
v.s: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.
v.c: Again, you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.

q: (after you have seen the reality of the Aakhirah)
you will definitely be questioned about the bounties

(the luxuries and talents Allaah has given you. You will be asked how you used them and whether you expressed gratitude for them) (A Hadith states that on the Day of Qiyaamah, man will be brought forward like a lamb. He will then be presented before Allaah, Who will ask, “Did I not grant you wealth and bounties? What did you do with these?” He will reply, “I accumulated it and multiplied it until it flourished. Then I left it all behind. Allow me to return and bring it all before you.” “Allaah will say, “Show Me what you had sent ahead here [to the Aakhirah as good deeds].” He will again reply, “I accumulated my wealth and multiplied it until it flourished. Then I left it all behind. Allow me to return and bring it all before you.” When it is clear that he had not performed any good deeds on earth, he will be flung into Jahannam.)
v.s: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure.
v.c: Then, on that Day, you will definitely be questioned about ˹your worldly˺ pleasures.
